sources.entry: Text Generation Web UI - An open-source web-based interface for running and managing language models locally, with support for a range of models, including LLaMA, GPT-J, and others. This tool is popular for experimentation and customization of LLMs without relying on cloud infrastructure.

summary.one_liner: TextGen (oobabooga/text-generation-webui) is an open-source desktop app and web UI for running local LLMs, with chat, vision, tool-calling, training, and an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a local LLM app with portable builds for Linux, Windows, and macOS (CUDA, Vulkan, ROCm, or CPU-only) that runs GGUF models through llama.cpp. Additional backends include ik_llama.cpp, Transformers, ExLlamaV3, and TensorRT-LLM, which require the full installation. The chat interface supports instruct, chat-instruct, and chat modes with Jinja2 prompt templates, image and PDF/.docx/text attachments, message branching, and a Notebook tab for free-form generation. It offers an OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API with tool-calling, where each tool is a single .py file and MCP servers are supported. The project also includes LoRA training and a diffusers-based image generation tab, plus extensions for TTS, voice input, and translation. The README states it runs 100% offline with no telemetry.
use_cases: run LLMs locally without cloud services
chat with local models and custom characters
local drop-in replacement for OpenAI or Anthropic API
fine-tune LoRAs on chat or text datasets
chat with PDFs and documents offline
local image generation with diffusers models
how_to_run: Download the portable build, unzip, and double-click `textgen` (desktop app)
git clone the repository and run: python -m venv venv
Or use the one-click start_windows.bat / start_linux.sh / start_macos.sh scripts
Or use Docker: docker compose up --build (after linking the appropriate docker files)
notable: Runs GGUF models from a user_data/models folder with automatic detection
OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible API with tool-calling and MCP support
Privacy-focused: offline, no telemetry, no remote update requests
Image generation tab with quantization and persistent gallery
caveats: Full installation (Transformers, EXL3, training, image generation) requires about 10GB disk space and downloads PyTorch; the portable build does not include these formats
Training is hidden in portable mode
Some backends depend on the platform and hardware; CPU-only training is described as extremely slow
